# Chasm

> Chasm gives each coding agent its own persistent Linux VM on hardware you control. Each sandbox is a full Incus/QEMU VM on KVM with its own guest kernel, private root disk and /workspace volume, plus a /shared volume mounted in every sandbox. Sandboxes keep their state across stop and start and are meant to run for weeks. Chasm runs on one Linux x86_64 host and needs no cloud service.

Key facts:
- Commands: `chasm create NAME`, `chasm start NAME`, `chasm shell NAME`, `chasm exec NAME -- CMD` (exit status preserved, separate stdout/stderr), `chasm stop`, `chasm pause`/`resume`, `chasm delete`, `chasm doctor --json`.
- Tested hosts: Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04, Fedora 45 (SELinux enforcing), Arch Linux; x86_64 with KVM. Hosts outside the Debian family need `--allow-untested-host`.
- Isolation: VM boundary per sandbox; an nftables policy blocks private and reserved IPv4 and routed IPv6 from guests; public IPv4 egress is not filtered.
- Not a hosted platform: no multi-host scheduling, public URLs, idle sleep with wake-on-request, or checkpoints today. It does not aim to replace Fly.io.
- License: MIT.
